Question
========
Why do modern systems use huge pages (e.g. 2 MB instead of 4 KB)?


Answerlist
----------
* It reduces the number of TLB entries needed to cover the same amount of memory
* It reduces the amount of internal fragmentation
* It reduces the depth of the page table walk
* It makes DRAM access itself faster

Solution
========
One huge page replaces 512 normal pages: a single TLB entry now covers 2 MB instead of 4 KB, and one level of the page table walk disappears. The cost is that a partially used huge page wastes much more memory.

Answerlist
----------
* 1. One entry covers 2 MB instead of 4 KB, so the TLB reach grows by a factor of 512.
* 0. The opposite: a barely used 2 MB page wastes far more than a 4 KB one.
* 1. The last level of the table is not needed any more.
* 0. The DRAM timings are unchanged; only the translation is cheaper.
